title: bandwidth-aware-prefill-sentinel-and-dynamic-kernel-throttle-for-paged-attention
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: Under mixed-tenant load the paged KV cache thrashes: large bursts cause aggressive kernel selection that favors throughput at the cost of long tail decode latency and frequent fragment eviction. Existing prefill heuristics are blind to cross-tenant bandwidth pressure and to the transient cost of switching kernel implementations. Goal: implement a bandwidth-aware prefill sentinel that coordinates multi-wave prefill passes and a dynamic kernel throttle that favors stable residency and bounded decode tail while preserving overall throughput and unit-cost efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: P99 decode latency for mixed tenant benchmark reduced by >= 18% in simulation compared to baseline
Sustained throughput loss <= 5% for heavy bursts after enabling the sentinel
No regression on single-tenant tight-latency benchmark (P50/P95 within 3% of baseline)
Automated e2e test coverage for multi-wave prefill and kernel-throttle states
Feature gated with runtime flag and rollout plan defined
engineering_notes: Sentinel watches per-shard metrics: page_touch_rate, decode_wave_size, resident_bytes, kernel_switch_count
Signal window: 250ms sliding window aggregated per-tenant and global. Tunable: window_ms=250
Multi-wave prefill: wave0 (conservative) marks high-touch spans with soft-reservations; wave1 (opportunistic) attempts fill under available bandwidth budget
Bandwidth budget: burst_quota per-shard computed from recent network+decode occupancy; quota decays with time-decay factor alpha=0.6
Kernel throttle: maintain moving average of kernel_switch_cost_ms; if switching cost > threshold and eviction_pressure high, prefer 'stable' kernel variants for next N requests
Eviction smoothing: implement decay-credit where recently-reserved spans gain rescue_credits; rescue triggers a low-cost fragment-restitch path rather than full-prefill when credit >= threshold
Data-structures: per-tenant LRU ring with priority buckets (hot/warm/cold) and soft-reserve boolean, track fingerprint for fragment-ids
Instrumentation: new tracing tags: prefill.wave, sentinel.action, kernel.throttle.state, rescue.credit
Flag gating: runtime.flag.prefill_sentinel (off by default), runtime.flag.kernel_throttle (off by default)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulation harness - implement simplified sentinel model in simulator; validate against existing production traces (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Runtime prototype behind flag - integrate small-state sentinel in runtime loop, ensure metrics and no regressions (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Controlled rollout - 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with canary metrics and automatic rollback (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Tuning and followups - tune thresholds and add micro-optimizations for kernel selection (ongoing)
tests: Unit: sentinel state transitions, budget decay math, rescue-credit accounting
Integration: end-to-end prefill flow with fake KV store and two kernel variants
Load: replay 24h of production traces with 10% synthetic burst amplification
Chaos: force kernel switch failure path and confirm fallback not causing unbounded eviction
rollout_plan: Enable flags in staging and run full replay tests
Canary on dedicated cluster (5% traffic) for 48 hours, monitor p99 and eviction metrics
Expand to 25% with longer observation window (7 days) and performance dashboards
Full rollout after thresholds met, leave auto-rollback threshold configured
risks: Mis-tuned budget could over-constrain throughput under legitimate high-load bursts
Kernel throttle could obscure root cause of performance regressions and make debugging harder
Complexity of rescue path may introduce correctness bugs for corner fragment layouts
Simulation mismatch: simulator may underrepresent cross-host scheduling delays
blockers: Need long-form production traces anonymized for simulator; SRE privacy approval pending
Benchmark harness dependency: ENG-551678 must land initial trace-replayer
Design sign-off from runtime leads required before flag-enabled prototype
